target_customer: Independent and collision auto repair shops
problem: Shops lose time on phone calls for insurance supplements, parts sourcing and customer updates; Parrot agents make and take those calls.
business_model: B2B software subscription, reported about $30,000 per shop per year in two early contracts
product_category: AI agents for auto repair operations

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice agents negotiating with insurers and vendors need reliability and integrations but build on commodity voice and LLM stacks.

defensibility.rationale: Vertical workflow knowledge could build switching costs, but nothing sourced shows it yet; a same batch rival CarSignal sells a $200 per month shop OS.

market_need_then: Two shops signed at $30,000 per year within three weeks of pivoting into collision repair, per one outlet.

branding.domain_note: Uses useparrot.com, a use prefix, implying the plain .com was unavailable (inference from domain only)

brand_strength.rationale: Brand sources found were for unrelated Parrot companies; name shares space with Parrot drones and Parrot AI.

pivots.to: AI agents for collision repair shops
pivots.why: pivoted about three weeks before Demo Day per RuntimeWire; month approximate

outcome_analysis: Parrot is a Spring 2026 company that pivoted from biomedical research workflows into collision repair shortly before Demo Day and reported two shop contracts at $30,000 a year. Funding is unverified and the company is too new for an outcome call.
notes: Funding unverified: Dealroom lists $125K seed, VCBacked and FundedIQ list $500K pre-seed in June 2026; no primary source, so no round recorded. RuntimeWire article was paywalled preview; founder backgrounds unknown. Pivot month approximate. Competitors dated at batch not found. CarSignal is a different company.
